He played college basketball for the [[UCF Knights men's basketball|UCF Knights]], transferring to UCF after completing his sophomore season for the [[2015–16 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2015–16 Michigan Wolverines]]. He is the son of [[Johnny Dawkins]] who became the UCF coach following the [[2015–16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. Dawkins was raised in North Carolina until spending his high school years in [[Northern California]] at [[Saint Francis High School (Mountain View)|St. Francis High School]] and [[Palo Alto High School]] and a [[postgraduate year]] in [[New England]] at [[New Hampton Prep]]. As a collegiate freshman for the [[2014–15 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2014–15 Wolverines]], he began the season on the bench, but became a starter when injuries plagued the team in January 2015. In his more prominent role later in the season, Dawkins led the [[2014–15 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2014–15 Big Ten Conference]] in [[effective field goal percentage]] and [[true shooting percentage]] during conference play. ==Early life== Dawkins was born in [[Durham, North Carolina]], the youngest of the four children of Tracy and [[Johnny Dawkins]].{{cite web|url=http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2014/06/johnny_dawkins_aubrey_dawkins.html|title=Johnny Dawkins finds pride in his son, Aubrey Dawkins, paving his own road to Michigan|access-date=March 12, 2015|date=June 30, 2014|work=[[MLive.com]]|author=Quinn, Brendan F.}}{{cite web|url=http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/aubrey_dawkins_909849.html|title=Aubrey Dawkins 24|access-date=March 12, 2015|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170629191247/http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/aubrey_dawkins_909849.html|archive-date=June 29, 2017|url-status=dead}} The elder Dawkins spent 11 years on [[Mike Krzyzewski]]'s coaching staff at [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]]. The family moved to California in 2008 when his father became the [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball]] head coach. Dawkins was a freshman at [[Saint Francis High School (Mountain View)|St. Francis High School]] of [[Mountain View, California]] in 2009. By the time he began his sophomore season he stood at {{convert|5|ft|8|in|m}}. As a junior, Dawkins transferred to [[Palo Alto High School]] in [[Palo Alto, California]]. That year he earned 2012 All-''[[San Jose Mercury News]]'' boys basketball third team recognition.{{cite web|url=http://www.mercurynews.com/ci_20346174/2012-all-daily-news-boys-basketball-teams|title=The 2012 All-Daily News Boys Basketball Teams|access-date=March 19, 2015|date=April 6, 2012|work=[[San Jose Mercury News]]}} As a senior, he stood at {{convert|6|ft|5|in|m}}, By January of his senior season he had not received any scholarship offers.{{cite web|url=http://www.sfgate.com/preps/article/High-school-stars-in-MLK-Classic-4207326.php|title=High school stars in MLK Classic|access-date=March 13, 2015|date=January 18, 2013|work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]|author=Stephens, Mitch}} That year he averaged 18.8 points and 7.0 rebounds and was on the 2013 All-''San Jose Mercury News'' boys basketball first team along with [[Aaron Gordon]].{{cite web|url=http://www.mercurynews.com/ci_22945279/all-mercury-news-boys-basketball-team|title=All-Mercury News boys basketball team|access-date=March 13, 2015|date=April 3, 2013|work=[[San Jose Mercury News]]}} After graduating, Dawkins did a [[postgraduate year]] at the [[New Hampton School]] in [[New Hampton, New Hampshire]] where he averaged 12.3 points and 3.6 rebounds before receiving a late scholarship offer from Michigan. His grades were not sufficient to pursue a scholarship at Stanford and despite his relationship with [[Chris Collins (basketball)|Chris Collins]], Northwestern was not interested in Dawkins given their commitments from wings Vic Law and Scottie Lindsey.{{cite web|url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-aubrey-dawkins-big-ten-bits-spt-0313-20150312-story.html|title=Freshman Aubrey Dawkins rewarding Michigan for giving him a chance|access-date=March 13, 2015|date=March 12, 2015|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Greenstein, Teddy and Shannon Ryan}} While at New Hampton, he was being recruited by [[Steve Donahue]] of [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Boston College]], but Donahue left Boston College in 2014 and recommended Dawkins to Beilein. Before Michigan stepped in, it appeared that he would have committed to [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton]],{{cite web|url=http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/022715aaa.html|title=Kornacki: Dawkins, Rahk Provide Story of Hoops Serendipity|access-date=March 12, 2015|date=February 27, 2015|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|author=Kornacki, Steve}} although he was also considering [[Utah State Aggies men's basketball|Utah State]], [[Pepperdine Waves men's basketball|Pepperdine]] as well as [[Montana Grizzlies men's basketball|Montana]],{{cite web|url=http://www.sfgate.com/collegesports/article/Stanford-s-success-shows-benefit-of-sticking-5345808.php|title=Stanford's success shows benefit of sticking together|access-date=March 13, 2015|date=March 25, 2014|work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]|author=Killion, Ann}} and [[Rhode Island Rams men's basketball|Rhode Island]] was showing a strong interest. In fact, during the [[2014 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]], Dawkins attended the Sweet 16 round to watch his father's [[2013–14 Stanford Cardinal men's basketball team|Stanford Cardinal]] play [[2013–14 Dayton Flyers men's basketball team|Dayton]] in the South Regional on March 27.{{cite web|url=http://www.mercurynews.com/california/ci_25412083/|title=Stanford prepares for Sweet 16 vs. Dayton|access-date=March 19, 2015|date=March 24, 2014|work=[[San Jose Mercury News]]|author=Dubow, Josh}} Dawkins accepted a recruiting visit to Michigan in early April 2014 when he received his scholarship offer.
